questions.q: What does Setup Audit Trail record?
options: Changes to record field values, like Opportunity Stage or Account Industry
Configuration changes made in Setup — permission sets, profiles, security settings, Apex classes, Flow versions, and more — with who made each change and when
Every report and dashboard a user has ever viewed
The content of every email sent through the org
questions.explain: Setup Audit Trail tracks configuration changes in Setup, not record data — each entry shows the Date, User, and Action for a change like a permission set edit or security setting update.

questions.q: How much setup change history does Setup Audit Trail retain, and how is older history accessed?
options: The on-screen view shows the most recent entries, but a download link provides the full six months of history as a CSV
Only the last 20 changes ever, with no way to see further back
Setup Audit Trail retains history forever, with unlimited on-screen scrolling
Two years, accessible only through a support ticket
questions.explain: Setup Audit Trail displays the most recent entries on screen, but an admin can download the full six months of setup change history as a CSV file.

questions.q: What does a row in Login History show?
options: Only whether a login succeeded, with no other detail
The user's current session timeout setting
Username, Login Time, Source IP, Location, Login Type, Status, Browser, and Platform for each login attempt
A list of every page the user visited after logging in
questions.explain: Login History records per-attempt detail — username, time, source IP, location, login type, success/failure status, browser, and platform.

questions.q: Why can't Login History or Setup Audit Trail answer 'who changed the Stage field on this Opportunity record'?
options: They can — all three tools track exactly the same information
Because Opportunity records are excluded from all monitoring tools
Because only System Administrators can view that information anywhere
Because neither tracks changes to record field data — that's what Field History Tracking (covered in Chapter 3) is for
questions.explain: Setup Audit Trail tracks configuration changes and Login History tracks login attempts — neither tracks record field data. Field History Tracking is the separate tool for that question.

questions.q: A user says a Flow stopped working, and an admin suspects someone changed a validation rule by accident. Which tool answers that question?
options: Login History, since the change was made during a login session
Setup Audit Trail, since changing a validation rule is a configuration change in Setup
Field History Tracking, since a validation rule is a type of field
None of these tools can show configuration changes
questions.explain: A validation rule edit is a Setup configuration change, which is exactly what Setup Audit Trail records — who changed it and when.
